title: Single-component twisted $\mathbb{Z}_3$ orthogonal metal in an $e/3$-anyon fluid
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Ashvin Vishwanath, Eslam Khalaf
abstract: We propose an unconventional metallic phase emerging on doping the $1/3$ Fractional Chern insulator, which can serve as a parent state to anyon superconductivity with arbitrary chiral central charge. It is a twisted $\mathbb{Z}_3$ orthogonal metal: a state with vanishing electron quasiparticle weight but a single well-defined Fermi surface of emergent charge-$e/3$ fermions coupled to a Dijkgraaf-Witten twisted $\mathbb{Z}_3$ gauge field. It is manifestly valley-symmetric and valley-gapped. Pairing this fractionalized Fermi surface then removes the topological order and produces a family of superconductors whose chiral central charge is directly set by the BdG band topology of the paired $e/3$ fermions, while the angular momentum of the physical order parameter is constrained to be a multiple of three. This scenario provides a route to superconducting states beyond anyon-superconductivity constructions based on $2e/3$ anyons. The metallic phase itself carries distinctive ``fractional Fermiology'' signatures: $e/3$ shot noise, anomalous quantum oscillations, and a $6π$ ac Josephson effect when it mediates the Josephson coupling between superconductors. We construct explicit wavefunction ansatz realizing the phase, and argue that inter-valley repulsion between anyons stabilizes this phase compared to competing states. We show that the construction extends to higher Laughlin states but not to Jain states.
summary: This work introduces a theoretical model for a twisted $\mathbb{Z}_3$ orthogonal metal formed by doping a Fractional Chern Insulator. The metallic phase is characterized by emergent $e/3$ fermions and exhibits unique transport signatures like fractional shot noise. Crucially, pairing this state allows the realization of superconducting phases whose topological properties are controllable via band structure analysis.
main_problem: The paper proposes an unconventional metallic phase, a twisted $\mathbb{Z}_3$ orthogonal metal, emerging when doping a Fractional Chern Insulator (FCI). This state serves as a parent for realizing anyon superconductivity with arbitrary chiral central charge.
main_result: The resulting metal exhibits fractionalized transport signatures ($e/3$ shot noise, $6\pi$ Josephson effect) and can pair into superconductors whose topological properties are dictated by the BdG band topology of the paired fermions.
method: The analysis uses parton decomposition on a low-energy Lagrangian derived from the parent FCI state to separate physics into itinerant (f) and gapped (g) sectors, followed by detailed theoretical predictions for transport and pairing.
model_or_system: The system models doping the $1/3$ Laughlin state on a lattice, characterized by three degenerate valleys due to fractional background flux. The effective low-energy theory is described by an interacting Lagrangian involving emergent charge-$e/3$ fermions coupled to a $\mathbb{Z}_3$ gauge field.
key_observables: Fractional charge ($e/3$), anomalous quantum oscillations (frequency factor of 9), $6\pi$ ac Josephson effect, and the chiral central charge ($c_{-}$) of the resulting superconductor.
important_parameters: Doping parameter ($\delta$), temperature regimes relative to localization scale ($T_{loc}$) and degeneracy scale ($T_d$), and the ratio of inter-valley to intra-valley repulsions ($r$).
main_assumptions: The stability of the single-pocket OM is argued based on net inter-valley repulsion, and the analysis assumes that the f-fermion sector governs low-energy charge dynamics.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows a $\delta$-$T$ phase diagram illustrating critical temperatures for different metallic and superconducting phases.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the parent state (FCI) and then uses parton decomposition to derive an effective Lagrangian. It analyzes transport properties, predicts fractionalized signatures, discusses competing metallic states (triple-pocket vs. single-pocket OM), and finally details how pairing leads to specific superconducting topological orders.
why_interesting: The explicit prediction of fractional charge carriers ($e/3$) and the connection between orbital magnetism, fractionalization, and tunable chiral central charges are highly relevant for designing novel topological quantum materials.
